title.narrative: F24AS00060 PROTECTING AND CONSERVING AFRICAN ELEPHANT PRIORITY POPULATIONS - 2024

description.narrative: THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO SUPPORT A RANGE-WIDE ELEPHANT CONSERVATION EFFORT BY CONTRIBUTING TO THE LARGEST EVIDENCE BASE ON AFRICAN ELEPHANT POPULATION TRENDS AND HUMAN-ELEPHANT CONFLICT (HEC) INTERVENTIONS. THE INTERNATIONAL UNION FOR CONSERVATION OF NATURE (IUCN) SPECIES SURVIVAL COMMISSIONS (SSC) AFRICAN ELEPHANT SPECIALIST GROUP (AFESG) SERVES AS THE WORLDS TECHNICAL AUTHORITY ON AFRICAN ELEPHANTS AND CONSISTS OF 95 EXPERT MEMBERS. THE AFESG PLAYS A UNIQUE ROLE AS A PROVIDER OF IMPARTIAL TECHNICAL ADVICE ON ALL ASPECTS OF ELEPHANT CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT TO A WIDE ARRAY OF STAKEHOLDERS. SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES INCLUDE: (1) MANAGING AND OPTIMIZING THE MOST COMPREHENSIVE REPOSITORY OF POPULATION-BASED DATA AND INFORMATION ON AFRICAN FOREST AND SAVANNA ELEPHANTS (THE AFRICAN ELEPHANT DATABASE) (2) REASSESSING FOREST AND SAVANNA ELEPHANT EXTINCTION RISK VIA THE IUCN RED LIST PROCESS AND ASSESSING THEIR RECOVERY STATUS FOR THE FIRST TIME VIA THE IUCN GREEN STATUS ASSESSMENT OF SPECIES (3) PROVIDING A RANGE-WIDE BASELINE OF HEC RISK, INCORPORATED IN TOOLKITS, GUIDELINES, AND CURRICULA (4) CONDUCTING COMPREHENSIVE SYNTHESES OF CONSERVATION-CRITICAL PATTERNS AND TRENDS INVOLVING EMERGING AFRICAN SCIENTISTS AND (5) PROVIDING TECHNICAL REPORTS AND INDEPENDENT TECHNICAL REVIEWS, INCLUDING THOSE MANDATED UN
